title: Environmental-Like Microplastic & Nanoplastic (eMNPs) Visualization and Characterization: Challenges and Future Outlooks
content: While most studies investigating the physicochemical properties and toxicity of micro and nanoplastics (MNPs) use manufactured plastic particles—typically spherical, uniform in size, and with homogeneous charge—real-world MNPs exhibit practically opposed properties of highly heterogeneous and irregular characteristics. This makes the analysis complicated whether they are found in the environment or synthesized in the laboratory.
